So I see a number of misunderstandings about the situation in Pharma when a branded drug increases their prices. I'll try to keep this brief. Disclosure: I used to work with formularies and their electronic data for pharmacy benefit managers.

  1. This drug is off patent (patents last only 20 years at maximum. They can be shortened by paragraph IV challenges here). Thus generics will not only likely exist, but would have been on sale for years already.
  2. Here is a list of alternatives covered by Blue Cross Blue Shield. I am no pharmacist/doctor, and would love to get input as to whether these are true chemical equivalents. [see edit below, I'll text my pharmacist friends to see if they have input].
  3. If insurers see this rise in price, there is no way in hell they will cover it when alternatives exist. The out of pocket prices for it will increase further.
  4. Doctors that look after their patients' financial stability should see this increase and prescribe alternatives. Generics could also be substituted (and the savings passed on to the patient) if the doctor does not mark the prescription as dispense as written.
  5. Competitors will see this as a huge opportunity for undercutting. Big Pharma and hundreds of small biotech companies are likely licking their lips at the business opportunity to create a drug with a small margin and undercut his price massively until it goes to something reasonable.

TL;DR This drug is off patent, has alternatives and will likely see its price and sales crash. He'll probably still make big money while others get cracking to jump in on the alternatives action.
